# Data overview

Libraries and loading data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(viridis)
library(rstatix)

reports <- read.csv("https://zenodo.org/records/10573715/files/CSE_student_performances%20%281%29.csv")
```

## Student Profile

Student Age, visible by Gender

```{r}
age_data <- reports %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(Gender))

age_min <- floor(min(age_data$Age))
age_max <- ceiling(max(age_data$Age))
bin_size <- 1

# Assorting groups shown in the dropdown
groups <- c("All students", unique(as.character(age_data$Gender)))

# Creating one histogram trace per group
student_demo_plot <- plot_ly()

for (i in seq_along(groups)) {
  
  group_name <- groups[i]
  
  group_data <- if (group_name == "All students") {
    age_data
  } else {
    filter(age_data, as.character(Gender) == group_name)
  }
  
  student_demo_plot <- add_trace(
    student_demo_plot,
    data = group_data,
    x = ~Age,
    type = "histogram",
    name = group_name,
    visible = i == 1,
    opacity = 0.85,
    xbins = list(
      start = age_min,
      end = age_max + 1,
      size = bin_size
    ),
    marker = list(
      color = viridis(length(groups), option = "D")[i]
    ),
    hovertemplate = paste(
      "Age: %{x}",
      "<br>Students: %{y}",
      "<extra></extra>"
    )
  )
}

# Adding dropdown menu
visibility <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
  as.list(seq_along(groups) == i)
})

dropdown_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(
      list(visible = visibility[[i]]),
      list(title = paste("Age Distribution:", groups[i]))
    ),
    label = groups[i]
  )
})

# Setting plot details
student_demo_plot <- student_demo_plot %>%
  layout(
    title = "Age Distribution: All students",
    bargap = 0.2,
    margin = list(t = 100),
    template = "plotly_white",
    xaxis = list(title = "Age"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of students"),
    updatemenus = list(
      list(
        type = "dropdown",
        buttons = dropdown_buttons,
        x = 1,
        y = 1.18,
        xanchor = "right"
      )
    ),
    margin = list(t = 100)
  )

student_demo_plot
```

## Study Habits

Academic Performance in relation to Taking Notes in Class: Table

```{r}
library(dplyr)

reports %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AcademicPerformance),
    !is.na(TakingNoteInClass)
  ) %>%
  count(AcademicPerformance, TakingNoteInClass) %>%
  group_by(AcademicPerformance) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(AcademicPerformance, TakingNoteInClass)

```

Academic Performance in relation to Taking Notes in Class: Dynamic Plot

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)

# Counting number of students in each combination
habit_data <- reports %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(TakingNoteInClass),
    !is.na(AcademicPerformance)
  ) %>%
  count(AcademicPerformance, TakingNoteInClass, name = "Students") %>%
  group_by(AcademicPerformance) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = 100 * Students / sum(Students)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Preserve the original category order 
performance_levels <- unique(reports$AcademicPerformance)
habit_data$AcademicPerformance <- factor(
  habit_data$AcademicPerformance,
  levels = performance_levels
)

# Animate between performance categories
animated_figure <- plot_ly(
  data = habit_data,
  x = ~TakingNoteInClass,
  y = ~Percentage,
  frame = ~AcademicPerformance,
  type = "bar",
  color = ~TakingNoteInClass,
  text = ~paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%"),
  textposition = "outside",
  hovertemplate = paste(
    "Note-taking: %{x}",
    "<br>Percentage: %{y:.1f}%",
    "<extra></extra>"
  )
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Note-taking Habits Across Academic Performance Groups",
    xaxis = list(title = "Do you take notes in class?"),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Percentage of Students (%)",
      range = c(0, 110)
    ),
    barmode = "group"
  ) %>%
  animation_opts(
    frame = 1000,
    transition = 500,
    redraw = TRUE
  ) %>%
  animation_button() %>%
  animation_slider()
```

## Sleep duration across academic performance groups

### **Question 1: Is daily sleep duration associated with self-reported academic performance among students?**

H~0~ - Sleep duration does not differ systematically across the four academic performance groups.

H~1~ - Sleep duration differs across at least two academic performance groups.

```{r}

#comparing individual sleep durations across performance groups

sleep_performance <- reports %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(SleepPerDayHours),
    !is.na(AcademicPerformance)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    AcademicPerformance = factor(
      AcademicPerformance,
      levels = c("Below average", "Average", "Good", "Excellent")
    ),
    PerformancePosition = as.numeric(AcademicPerformance)
  )

#calculate group medians and sample sizes

sleep_group_summary <- sleep_performance %>%
  group_by(AcademicPerformance, PerformancePosition) %>%
  summarise(
    MedianSleep = median(SleepPerDayHours),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#add slight horizontal jitter so overlapping observations are visible

set.seed(123)

sleep_performance <- sleep_performance %>%
  mutate(
    JitteredPosition = PerformancePosition +
      runif(n(), -0.12, 0.12)
  )

#interactive dot plot

plot_ly() %>%
  add_trace(
    data = sleep_performance,
    x = ~JitteredPosition,
    y = ~SleepPerDayHours,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",
    color = ~AcademicPerformance,
    colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE725"),
    marker = list(size = 9, opacity = 0.7),
    text = ~paste0(
      "Performance: ", AcademicPerformance,
      "<br>Sleep: ", SleepPerDayHours, " hours"
    ),
    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    name = "Individual students"
  ) %>%
  add_trace(
    data = sleep_group_summary,
    x = ~PerformancePosition,
    y = ~MedianSleep,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",
    marker = list(
      symbol = "diamond",
      size = 15,
      color = "black",
      line = list(color = "white", width = 1)
    ),
    text = ~paste0(
      "Performance: ", AcademicPerformance,
      "<br>Median sleep: ", MedianSleep, " hours",
      "<br>Number of students: ", N
    ),
    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    name = "Group median"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "Sleep duration across academic performance groups"
    ),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Academic performance",
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = 1:4,
      ticktext = c(
        "Below average", "Average", "Good", "Excellent"
      ),
      range = c(0.5, 4.5)
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Hours of sleep per day",
      dtick = 1
    ),
    margin = list(b = 90, t = 80),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2)
  )

```

### 

#### Statistical analysis: Sleep and academic performance

```{r}
#Kruskal-Wallis test to compare sleep duration across performance groups
sleep_test <- kruskal.test(
  SleepPerDayHours ~ AcademicPerformance,
  data = sleep_performance
)

sleep_test

```

#interpretation and move onto:

#### Which groups differ?

```{r}
#pairwise comparisons between academic performance groups
rstatix::dunn_test(
  data = sleep_performance,
  SleepPerDayHours ~ AcademicPerformance,
  p.adjust.method = "holm"
)
```

Holm-adjusted Dunn tests indicated significant differences in sleep duration between the *Below average* and *Excellent* performance groups (p = .028), and between the *Good* and *Excellent* groups (p = .048). The other pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant after correcting for multiple comparisons. These findings suggest that sleep duration differed between some, but not all, academic performance groups. However, the small sample sizes in the *Below average* (n = 4) and *Excellent* (n = 9) groups warrant caution when interpreting these differences.

#### Effect size

```{r}
#calculate effect size for the Kruskal-Wallis test
H <- as.numeric(sleep_test$statistic)
k <- 4
n <- nrow(sleep_performance)

epsilon_squared <- max(0, (H - k + 1) / (n - k))

epsilon_squared
```

The estimated epsilon-squared effect size was (0.108), suggesting some differences in sleep-duration distributions across academic performance groups. This complements the significant Kruskal–Wallis result, although the estimate should be interpreted cautiously given the small and unequal group sizes.

## Sleep duration across self-reported depression-status groups

### **Question 2: Is daily sleep duration associated with self-reported depression status among students?**

H~0~ - Sleep duration does not differ systematically between the depression-status groups.

H~1~ - Sleep duration differs across at least two depression-status groups.

```{r}
#prepare data for the sleep and well-being analysis
sleep_wellbeing <- reports %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(SleepPerDayHours),
    !is.na(DepressionStatus)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    DepressionStatus = factor(
      trimws(as.character(DepressionStatus)),
      levels = c("No", "Sometimes", "Yes")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(DepressionStatus))

#summarise sleep duration by depression status
sleep_wellbeing %>%
  group_by(DepressionStatus) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    MedianSleep = median(SleepPerDayHours),
    IQR = IQR(SleepPerDayHours),
    MeanSleep = mean(SleepPerDayHours),
    SD = sd(SleepPerDayHours),
    .groups = "drop"
  )



# Calculate group medians and sample sizes
  wellbeing_summary <- sleep_wellbeing %>%
    group_by(DepressionStatus) %>%
    summarise(
      MedianSleep = median(SleepPerDayHours),
      N = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(GroupPosition = as.numeric(DepressionStatus))
  
  # Add slight horizontal jitter to separate overlapping points
  set.seed(123)
  
  sleep_wellbeing <- sleep_wellbeing %>%
    mutate(
      GroupPosition = as.numeric(DepressionStatus),
      JitteredPosition = GroupPosition + runif(n(), -0.12, 0.12)
    )
  
  # Interactive dot plot
  plot_ly() %>%
    add_trace(
      data = sleep_wellbeing,
      x = ~JitteredPosition,
      y = ~SleepPerDayHours,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "markers",
      color = ~DepressionStatus,
      colors = c("#440154", "#21918C", "#FDE725"),
      marker = list(size = 9, opacity = 0.7),
      text = ~paste0(
        "Depression status: ", DepressionStatus,
        "<br>Sleep duration: ", SleepPerDayHours, " hours"
      ),
      hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
      name = "Individual students"
    ) %>%
    add_trace(
      data = wellbeing_summary,
      x = ~GroupPosition,
      y = ~MedianSleep,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "markers",
      marker = list(
        symbol = "diamond",
        size = 15,
        color = "black",
        line = list(color = "white", width = 1)
      ),
      text = ~paste0(
        "Depression status: ", DepressionStatus,
        "<br>Median sleep: ", MedianSleep, " hours",
        "<br>Number of students: ", N
      ),
      hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
      name = "Group median"
    ) %>%
    layout(
      title = list(
        text = "Sleep duration across depression-status groups"
      ),
      xaxis = list(
        title = "Self-reported depression status",
        tickmode = "array",
        tickvals = 1:3,
        ticktext = c("No", "Sometimes", "Yes"),
        range = c(0.5, 3.5)
      ),
      yaxis = list(
        title = "Hours of sleep per day",
        dtick = 1
      ),
      margin = list(b = 90, t = 80),
      legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2)
    )
  
```

#### **Statistical Analysis: Sleep and Well-being**

```{r}
#test whether sleep duration differs across depression-status groups
wellbeing_test <- kruskal.test(
  SleepPerDayHours ~ DepressionStatus,
  data = sleep_wellbeing
)

wellbeing_test
```

(interpretation)

#### Which groups differ?

```{r}
#pairwise comparisons with Holm correction
wellbeing_pairwise <- rstatix::dunn_test(
  data = sleep_wellbeing,
  SleepPerDayHours ~ DepressionStatus,
  p.adjust.method = "holm"
)

wellbeing_pairwise %>%
  select(group1, group2, n1, n2, statistic, p, p.adj)

```

(interpretation)

#### Effect size

```{r}
#calculate approximate epsilon-squared
H <- as.numeric(wellbeing_test$statistic)
k <- nlevels(droplevels(sleep_wellbeing$DepressionStatus))
n <- nrow(sleep_wellbeing)

epsilon_squared_wellbeing <- max(
  0, (H - k + 1) / (n - k)
)

epsilon_squared_wellbeing
```

(interpretation)

## Number of friends

```{r}
#descriptive statistics summary of variable friends data 
friend_summary <- reports %>%
  summarise(
    total_students = n(),
    valid_responses = sum(!is.na(NumberOfFriend)),
    missing_responses = sum(is.na(NumberOfFriend)),
    missing_percent = 100 * mean(is.na(NumberOfFriend)),
    mean_friends = mean(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_friends = sd(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_friends = median(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_friends = IQR(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum_friends = min(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_friends = max(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) 

#putting the statistics in a readable table
friend_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Statistic",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Statistic = gsub("_", " ", Statistic),
    Value = round(Value, 2)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Statistic", "Value"),
    caption = "Summary of number of friends"
  )


#plotting of distribution of number of friends

  data = reports,
  x = NumberOfFriend,
  xlab = "Number of friends",
  title = "How many friends do students have on average?",

  centrality.type = "mean",

    color = "black",

    linetype = "dashed"
  ),
  bin.args = list(
    fill = viridisLite::viridis(5)[3],
    color = "white"
  ),
  results.subtitle = FALSE,               
  ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_bw()        
)
```
